subject: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 8, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline

All —

We’re at the point where we need a crisp, cross-team definition of what “supported” means for the Private observability minimum pack (VPC + on-prem), and agreement on v1 requirements + timeline so we can message it and staff Support/SRE properly.

Request: please review the requirements + scope docs and reply with (a) approve/changes, (b) any non-negotiables from SRE/Telemetry/Platform, and (c) whether you’re comfortable with the proposed dates.

Docs / pointers:
- PRD / requirements (living): Confluence: /display/ENGPRIVATE/Private+observability+minimum+pack+requirements
- Scope ADR (what’s in/out): Confluence: /display/ARCH/ADR-021+Private+observability+minimum+pack+scope
- Log pipeline defaults ADR: Confluence: /display/ARCH/ADR-022+Log+pipeline+defaults+private
- Tracking ticket: Linear PM-842

Proposed v1 definition of “supported” (draft):
1) We ship a versioned, turnkey bundle via Helm + installer (dashboards + alert rules + log collector defaults) that installs without bespoke customer work in reference environments.
2) Alerts are aligned to SLO guidance (latency/availability) and include runbook links and “what to do first”.
3) Metrics naming/labeling follow the Private standards (bounded cardinality).
4) Log pipeline: structured logs + safe redaction defaults + at least one tested export path (Splunk HEC and/or ELK) + documented OTLP option if feasible.
5) Upgrade/rollback does not blank dashboards or break rules (or we provide explicit migration steps).

Proposed timeline (for GA-ready in the Private release train):
- Requirements freeze: Fri Jul 19
- Implementation complete (dashboards/rules/log pipeline wired into charts + installer): Fri Aug 23
- Validation (VPC + on-prem-like/air-gap): Aug 26 – Sep 6
- Support enablement + release notes: Sep 9 – Sep 13
- Target GA: Wed Sep 18

Open questions I want us to settle in this thread:
- Paging vs ticket-only: which alerts are page-worthy by default for Private? (SRE concern)
- Export targets: do we require OTLP for v1, or are Splunk HEC + ELK sufficient with OTLP documented as “experimental”?
- Minimum dashboard set: runtime overview + control plane health + “cluster resources” panels — any must-haves missing?

If easier, Talia can schedule a 30 min decision meeting, but I’m hoping we can align asynchronously.

Thanks,
Vivek
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 8, 2025 at 10:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline

Vivek — overall direction looks right. A few SRE non-negotiables / edits to the “supported” definition:

1) Alerting defaults: we cannot ship a pack that pages on day 1 in most customer clusters. For Private, defaults should be ticket-only for anything not clearly “service down” or “SLO burn at high rate”.
   - Page-worthy (default ON):
     - API gateway 5xx spike / availability SLO burn (fast burn)
     - Request latency p99 sustained + error rate elevated (fast burn)
     - Prometheus scrape/TSDB critical (Prometheus down / no scrapes for Redwood targets)
   - Ticket-only (default ON or OFF depending on noise):
     - GPU saturation, OOM kills, restart loops, disk pressure (often customer-driven sizing issues; should generate clear guidance, not pages)

2) Runbook links in alert annotations: please make this part of “supported”. We need consistent runbook URLs (even if they land on internal Confluence initially for Support; for customers we can later publish sanitized docs).

3) Cardinality: we should explicitly state which labels are allowed in Private. No raw tenant_id, no request_id as a label, and route/model labels must be bounded (top-N aggregation or hashed bucket) or moved to logs.

Timeline: Sep 18 GA is fine *if* we have at least 2 weeks of staging validation where SRE can review noise and tune thresholds. The Aug 26 – Sep 6 window is tight; if we slip, I’d rather slip GA than ship noisy rules.

- Neha
SRE / Observability

From: Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 8, 2025 at 11:24 AM PT
Subject: Re: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline

+1 to Neha’s points.

Two additions from standards/architecture:

A) “Supported” should include a compatibility contract:
- Metric names/recording rules used by dashboards must be versioned and either (1) remain backward compatible for at least one minor version or (2) have a documented migration.
- Dashboards and rules must be shipped as artifacts inside the Private installer/Helm release (air-gap constraint).

B) Log pipeline: I recommend we explicitly call out structured logging fields that are guaranteed and redacted.
- request_id allowed in logs, not metrics labels
- tenant_id must be hashed if included
- no request/response payload logging by default

On export targets: I’m comfortable with “tested sinks: Splunk HEC + Elasticsearch/OpenSearch” for v1, and OTLP as “supported as a protocol endpoint” only if we can validate in at least one reference environment. Otherwise, call OTLP “best effort” until we have CI coverage.

If you want, I can add a small “definition of supported” section directly to the ADR-021 so we have a single place to point to.

Allison
Observability Standards / Architecture

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 8, 2025 at 12:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline

Telemetry POV:

- Metric cardinality: we should enforce it in code/config, not just documentation. There are already PRs in flight to standardize/reduce labels for Private (see GitHub: redwood PR-18503) — we should treat that as a GA gating item.

- Dashboards: minimum set looks good if it includes:
  1) Runtime overview (latency + token throughput + batching + KV cache + GPU utilization)
  2) Control plane health (gateway/auth/policy/routing)
  3) “Scrape health” + TSDB health panels (so customers can self-diagnose why dashboards are empty)

- OTLP: from an engineering standpoint, it’s not a lot more to support OTLP logs export if we choose a collector that already speaks it, but validation is the issue. If SRE can’t validate, I’d rather not label it as supported.

Timeline: OK, but agree with Neha that we need time for tuning. We also need a clear “feature flag” for alerts so we can ship rules without enabling all of them by default.

Logan
Telemetry Platform Lead

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 8, 2025 at 1:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline

Approved directionally.

Conditions for calling this “supported”:
1) Bounded metrics cardinality enforced (Logan’s point). GA gate = merged + included in release branch.
2) Alerts must have conservative defaults (Neha’s point) and include runbook links.
3) Air-gap packaging must include dashboards + rules + collector config artifacts with checksums.
4) Validation must include at least one “tight NetworkPolicy” scenario (we have seen scrape failures in customer clusters).

On OTLP: do not make it a v1 requirement unless SRE signs off that it’s validated and documented. Splunk + ELK as tested exports is fine.

Timeline: Sep 18 GA is fine, but treat it as a target, not a promise. If the validation window shows noisy alerts or dashboards break on upgrade, we slip.

Priya
VP Engineering, Platform

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 9, 2025 at 4:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Private observability minimum pack — requirements review + definition of “supported” + launch timeline

Thanks all — summarizing decisions + actions so we’re aligned.

Decisions (capturing as the working definition of “supported” for v1):
- “Supported” = versioned bundle shipped via Helm + Private installer, validated in reference VPC + on-prem-like envs, with:
  - Minimum dashboards (runtime overview, control plane health, scrape/TSDB health)
  - Prometheus alert rules with conservative defaults + clear severities (page-worthy only for “service down / fast SLO burn”) + runbook links in annotations
  - Structured logs with redaction-safe defaults; tested exports to Splunk HEC + Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
  - Metrics naming/labels meet Private standards and cardinality is enforced (GA gating)
  - Upgrade/rollback safe (or migration doc)
- OTLP export: not required for v1. If we can validate it in CI/reference env, we’ll list it as supported; otherwise documented as “best effort/experimental”.
- GA date: Sep 18 remains the target, with explicit slip criteria (noise, upgrade breakage, or missing air-gap artifacts).

Action items:
1) Allison — please add a short “definition of supported” section to ADR-021 (or link to a single canonical section in the requirements doc). Due EOW.
2) Neha/Rafael — propose the default ON paging set vs ticket-only set + initial thresholds (tie to SLO burn where possible). Please drop into PM-842 and tag me + Talia. Due Jul 12.
3) Logan — confirm the cardinality enforcement GA gate + owner for the PR and follow-on release backport plan (redwood PR-18503). Due Jul 12.
4) Talia — set up a 30 min checkpoint the week of Aug 26 specifically for “alert noise + validation readiness” so we don’t discover issues at the end.
5) Vivek (me) — update the requirements doc with the above decisions and clarify OTLP language. I’ll do this today.

Tracking:
- PM-842 (program / acceptance criteria)
- ENG-19147 / ENG-19148 (alerts)
- ENG-19152 (Helm wiring)
- redwood-private-installer PR-18422 (preflight/postinstall validation)

If anyone disagrees with the summary, reply-all with corrections.

Vivek
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
